card.name: Digits inside numeric thresholds and doses
card.fires_on: A single digit (often 5, 0 or 4) that finishes or continues a number in dose, lab-limit or range text. Typical settings are 1.5 or 2.5 × ULN, 400 mg, and 100 mL.

modes.label: Decimal limits
modes.description: The 5 after a decimal point in multiples of the upper limit of normal or lab cutoffs.
modes.example: Either AST or ALT is >2.<<5>> x ULN Delay further DECNUP

modes.label: Round doses and volumes
modes.description: The final 0 of a number like 100 or 400 before mg or mL.
modes.example: the recommended maintenance regimen is 40<<0>> mg every four weeks.

modes.label: Durations and ranges
modes.description: A digit inside a duration or range of hours or weeks.
modes.example: In a 10<<4>>-week, open-label study in pediatric patients

card.writes: The promoted tokens are mostly Chinese counting words and unrelated fragments, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It fires on the last digits of numbers in lab limits, doses and study lengths.
